r1.title: A Day of the Ivorian Miracle
r1.intro: Build your base map at the museum, walk past the buildings of the Ivorian miracle, step into the contemporary art scene in the afternoon, and watch the lagoon from a historic hotel at dusk. The whole day stays in Plateau and Cocody, with no backtracking.
r1.transport: Ride-hailing within the area (Yango and others) is easiest. Plateau to Cocody is about 5 km: 1,200–1,800 FCFA off-peak, 1,800–2,500 FCFA at peak times.
r1.costNote: Excludes lunch and hotel drinks. Ride-hailing prices vary by time of day; Friday evening is the most expensive.

r2.title: The South Bank: Craft, Stage and Nightlife
r2.intro: The south bank of the lagoon is Abidjan at its most lived-in: Mandela's tailor has his workshop here, MASA builds its stage here, and Magic System grew up here.
r2.transport: Everything is in two neighbouring districts, so most rides are short.
r2.costNote: Excludes shopping. Restaurant prices in Zone 4 vary widely.

r3.title: Two Days on the Coast: Grand-Bassam and Assinie
r3.intro: East along the coast: on day one, walk the colonial streets of the first capital; on day two, go to the weekend beach of Abidjan's elite. From late October to early November you will catch the Abissa festival.
r3.transport: A private car or ride-hailing is easiest; you can also take a gbaka (minibus) from the Bassam station in Treichville, much cheaper but slower. The Abidjan–Grand-Bassam expressway is tolled.
r3.costNote: Estimated for one person in mid-range accommodation; two people can share the car. Transport to Assinie and the museum ticket are not yet verified.

r4.title: Three Days in the Heart of the Country: Yamoussoukro and Baoulé Land
r4.intro: North to the founding father's home town: on day one, the politics of grand projects; on day two, a Baoulé weaving village; on day three, where cocoa comes from.
r4.transport: Intercity buses are cheapest; get around locally by woro-woro or a private car. Fares may rise 20–30 per cent before holidays and at weekends.
r4.costNote: Only the bus fare on this route has been verified; other items will be added in the weekly updates.

r5.title: The Second Capital: Bingerville
r5.intro: In 1900 yellow fever drove the capital from Grand-Bassam up to this plateau. Today Bingerville is close to Cocody yet as quiet as another era: a colonial botanical garden, a museum in an art school, and a fishing village on the lagoon.
r5.transport: Ride-hailing from Cocody is easiest. Bingerville is small; take short rides between the garden and the museum.
r5.costNote: Ride costs are estimated from the quote for the roughly 5 km Plateau–Cocody trip and have not been tested.

stops: Founded in 1904 on the orders of Governor Angoulvant, about 56 hectares, where coffee and cocoa were first trialled in Côte d'Ivoire, with century-old trees. Go in daylight, in company, and ask staff to guide you: local reports have mentioned safety problems in the park.

r6.title: Three Days of Northern Craft: Korhogo and Senufo Land
r6.intro: A little over an hour's flight takes you from the lagoon city to the savannah. All three days are around Korhogo: weavers piecing strips into cloth, painters hand-painting animals on cotton, and blacksmiths smelting iron ore in clay furnaces.
r6.transport: Air Côte d'Ivoire direct flights save the most time; a local car with a guide is easiest. Long-distance buses run too, but the journey is long.
r6.costNote: Flights converted from about €61–129 one-way on comparison sites; prices vary by date.

r7.title: City of Eighteen Mountains: Man and the Dan World
r7.intro: The west is the coolest and greenest part of Côte d'Ivoire, and home to the mask culture of the Dan (Yacouba). All three days are around Man: waterfalls, the climb up the Dent de Man, the monkeys of the sacred forest, and with luck the stilt dancers.
r7.transport: Flying saves the most time; long-distance buses take 7 hours or more. Hire a car with a guide locally.
r7.costNote: The flight is the lowest return fare seen on Air Côte d'Ivoire's website; actual prices vary by date.

r8.title: Two Days at the Dakar Biennale
r8.intro: 'Abidjan has the money, Dakar has the taste': go and see for yourself. Both days are on the Dakar peninsula: the national Museum of Black Civilisations, the artists' village, Gorée Island, and the Dak'Art venues from 19 November.
r8.transport: Direct flights from Abidjan to Dakar. Ride-hailing or taxis in town; ferry to Gorée.
r8.costNote: Senegal also uses the West African CFA franc. The flight is the lowest return fare seen on Air Côte d'Ivoire's website and may be higher during the biennale.
